title: Chapter 129 — De-escalation
intro: When a customer is angry, your instinct is to defend. Override that instinct.

sections.title: The HEARD Method
sections.content: Hear: let them vent completely. Do not interrupt. Do not defend. Let the pressure out. Empathize: 'I would be frustrated too.' Name the emotion. Apologize: 'I am sorry this happened.' Even if it is not your fault — you are sorry they are experiencing it. Resolve: 'Here is what I am going to do right now.' Give them a specific action. Diagnose: after the emotion subsides, figure out what went wrong and how to prevent it.

sections.title: Lower Your Voice
sections.content:
When a customer raises their voice, lower yours. This is counterintuitive but it works. Matching their volume escalates the conflict. Dropping yours forces them to quiet down to hear you.

Slow down your speaking pace. Use shorter sentences. Make eye contact. Stay physically relaxed — uncrossed arms, open posture. Your calm is contagious.

sections.title: When to Escalate
sections.content:
Handle it yourself when: the customer is frustrated but reasonable, the resolution is within your authority, and you can solve it in one interaction.

Bring in a manager when: the customer demands it, the resolution requires authority you do not have, or the situation is becoming personal or abusive.

Never say 'that is not my department.' Own the problem even if someone else fixes it. 'Let me get the right person to help you — I will stay with you until this is resolved.'
